title: Back Titration Step-by-Step Diagram
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AP Chemistry
description: Four-step interactive diagram of a back titration: an antacid tablet is weighed, a known excess of HCl is added, the leftover HCl is titrated with NaOH, and the calcium carbonate content is calculated by subtraction. A slider changes the NaOH endpoint volume and every calculation line updates.

learningObjectives: Judge when a back titration is preferable to a direct titration
Calculate the amount of analyte from the reagent added, the reagent left over, and the mole ratios
standards: AP Chemistry CED Unit 4, Topic 4.6: Introduction to Titration

controls.label: Next Step
controls.description: Advances one step and reveals its calculation line

controls.label: NaOH at endpoint
controls.description: Volume of 0.2500 M NaOH needed to neutralize the leftover HCl, 5.00 to 40.00 mL in steps of 0.05

equations: n(HCl reacted) = n(HCl added) - n(HCl excess)
assumptions: Tablet mass 1.250 g, 50.00 mL of 0.5000 M HCl, 0.2500 M NaOH (chapter worked example)
Only CaCO3 in the tablet reacts with HCl

keyQuestions: Why is the excess reagent titrated instead of the analyte?
Why does a larger NaOH volume mean less CaCO3 in the tablet?
commonMisconceptions: Using the moles of NaOH directly as the moles of analyte
Forgetting to subtract the excess from the amount added
Applying the 2 to 1 mole ratio to the wrong quantity
assessmentOpportunities: Have students calculate each line before revealing it, then repeat with a different endpoint volume
